newsitem.title: POLAND: Early zloty rise sets off central bank dlr-buying.
newsitem.headline: Early zloty rise sets off central bank dlr-buying.

text.p: The Polish zloty hit resistance and a small central bank currency-buying intervention at 2.55 percent from the parity rate as the market's pro-zloty mood pushed the local unit higher in early trade, dealers said.

Dealers said the intervention again showed the central bank did not want to let the zloty strengthen back toward three percent from parity after spending nearly $300 million last week to knock the local currency down to 2.5 percent.
"The central bank seems set on keeping the zloty from firming against the basket, even if this means further interventions," said one dealer from a foreign bank in Warsaw.
At 0845 GMT the zloty was at 2.51/2.43 percent from parity, down from Friday's close and opening's 2.54/2.44 percent and morning highs around 2.55 percent from parity.
It was at 3.1280/05 to the dollar, down from 3.1270/00 at opening and at 1.8362/72 to the mark, flat from 1.8355/75.
The central bank bought about $10 million at 3.1265 zlotys.

Analysts said that the central bank weakened the zloty last week in order to prop up exports, while keeping real interest rates rising to cool import-boosting domestic demand, in order to keep the Poland's trade deficit from growing too quickly.
One-day deposit rates fell further on the overliquid money market after the central bank refrained from staging an open market operation on Monday, dealers said.
Overnight rates fell to 20.80/21.35 percent from opening's 21.25/21.40 percent and tomorrow/next fell to 20.80/21.15 percent from 21.40/21.60 at 0630 GMT.
Dealers said the central bank did not stage a drainage or NBP-bill sale today because such an offer would likely take bids from the treasury's 1.3 billion zloty T-bill tender.
